steps.title: Bigger bets, bigger falls
steps.body: Some people borrow to buy more of a share they believe in. Investing with borrowed money is called [[leverage]]. It makes every move bigger, up and down, and the loan stays the same size either way.

stat.label: your own money after a 30% fall, with as much borrowed as you own

steps.prompt: You invest €10,000 of your own and borrow more on top. Move the price: find a fall that wipes out all of your own money.

borrowed.label: Borrowed, as % of your own money

goal.hint: With as much borrowed as you own, the price only has to halve.

steps.prompt: A share is everywhere online. What do you do with €10,000 of savings? Pick one and jump 6 months ahead.

choices.label: All in, plus a €10,000 loan
choices.ending: The hype ended and the price crashed. The shares are worth €6,000, but the loan is still €10,000. You are €4,000 in debt.

choices.label: Only €1,000 you could afford to lose
choices.ending: You lost €700. It stings, but your savings are safe and you saw how hype works.

choices.label: Skip it
choices.ending: Nothing happened to your €10,000. Six months later, nobody talks about the share any more.

steps.prompt: You invest €10,000 of your own and €10,000 borrowed. The price falls 30%. What happens to your own money?
steps.explanation: You hold €20,000 of shares. A 30% fall is €6,000, and all of it comes out of your own money, because the loan is repaid in full.

steps.prompt: Which money can go into a risky bet without hurting your life?
options: Money you could lose completely and still pay rent and bills
Money borrowed at a low rate
steps.explanation: Your [[risk-capacity]] is what you could lose without it changing your daily life. Rent money and borrowed money are not part of it.

goal.hint: Leave “Borrowed” at 100% and set the price change to −50%.
